title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. The hesitation is itself the content: without a directedness or compatibility hypothesis on the figures, the system 𝔓(F̃) need not embed in a single power set. The page is fragmentary, so the exact status of 'pré-compatibles' cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Tame parts adapted to a figure F identify with 𝔓(F̃), the power set of its finite set of strata. A refinement F' ≪ F gives a surjection F̃' → F̃ and a pullback Boolean embedding 𝔓(F̃) → 𝔓(F̃').
ideas.modern_name: Directed system of finite Boolean algebras of cell/stratum unions (definable sets compatible with a cell decomposition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in o-minimality (van den Dries; Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn) and cell-complex combinatorics
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

ideas.what: Rather than assuming a global ambient set, realise all strata as subsets of a set P of 'points' via an axiomatised map M → 𝔓(P) (monotone, intersection, disjointness, additivity, T0).
ideas.modern_name: Stone-type representation / point-set realisation; analogous to type spaces or the o-minimal spectrum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936); in tame settings Coste–Roy (real spectrum), Pillay (1988, o-minimal spectrum)

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats 'points' as derived from a purely combinatorial stratified structure, via a Stone-like realisation subject to compatibility of figures. This parallels the later o-minimal spectrum / type-space approach (Pillay, Coste–Roy, Edmundo et al.). He also flags explicitly that incompatible figures obstruct a canonical common point set.
missed.quote: comme des parties d'un même ensemble 𝔓(P) disons, où P est un ensemble de "points"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a point-free foundation for tame topology. Points are a realisation of an abstract stratified structure, not primitive, which is relevant to locale- or Boolean-algebra-based treatments of o-minimal and tame geometry. The page alone is only a statement of intent, however.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting glimpse of a point-free, Stone-style foundation for Grothendieck's tame topology. But the mathematics on this page is routine: finite Boolean algebras under refinement plus an announced definition. Analogous spectra exist in the later model-theoretic literature.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed '⨍' / '\not P' is almost certainly 𝔓 (power set), consistent with page 73's 𝔓(P).
"rapports modérés" is more plausibly "parties modérées", and "l'un des rapports s'identifiant" more plausibly "l'ens. de ces parties s'identifiant à 𝔓(F̃)".
"réalisation par rapports" is likely "réalisation ponctuelle" (or "par parties").
"de façon unique" is likely "de façon cohérente".
